unbiased-ai.key_hint: Create an API key at platform.unbiased.ai (signup is reviewed by hand). Keys look like sk_...
unbiased-ai._note: OpenAI-compatible. The endpoint also answers Anthropic's /v1/messages and accepts either Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key, but the OpenAI pair is what llmproxy sends by default, so no 'protocol' is set. GET /v1/models is NOT available: an authenticated request returns 404 with code 'unknown_url' (unauthenticated, every path returns 401, because the gateway checks the key before routing — so a 401 here means no key, not a missing endpoint). Model discovery therefore finds nothing. This provider therefore ships example_model_filter ["pareto"], so config.example.json carries "model_filter": ["pareto"] and a copied example works as is: when a /models fetch fails, llmproxy synthesizes the model list from model_filter, which is the supported way to use a provider that publishes no catalog. A hand-written config still needs the filter set, or the provider contributes nothing. Pricing and limits, checked September 2026: one model, 'pareto', a blend of frontier and open models. Unbiased's own pricing page lists $2.50/Mtok input, $0.25/Mtok cached input and $7.50/Mtok output, and states that subscriptions (Personal, Personal Max, pay-as-you-go) carry a usage allowance rather than unlimited usage. There is NO free tier, so nothing here belongs in believed_free, free_limits or free_allowance: listing pareto as free would put a paid model at the front of the free rotation and bill real credits. No per-minute or per-day rate limits are published on the pricing page, the model card or the docs, so free_limits stays empty for lack of a figure rather than because the limits are unlimited. The per-token rates above match the 'openrouter/unbiased/pareto' entry already carried in the top-level pricing block (2.5e-06 / 7.5e-06), which is where paid rates live; that block is rebuilt each scraper run from the LiteLLM baseline plus live-source overrides, so a direct 'unbiased-ai/pareto' key hand-added there would not survive the next run.

kilo.key_hint: Create an API key at app.kilo.ai → Your Profile on your personal account (not an organization), then scroll to the bottom of the page. Requires account credits (docs: kilo.ai/docs/gateway)
kilo._note: OpenAI-compatible multi-vendor gateway. The base path is /api/gateway, not /v1, so discovery hits /api/gateway/models; that endpoint answers 200 without a key and returns an OpenRouter-shaped {"data": [...]} catalog (~380 models as of September 2026, ids like anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 and kilo-auto/* router pseudo-models), so no models_url override is needed. Inference is credit-based; some catalog entries carry an isFree flag, but no free tier is asserted here because none was observed in use.

modelscope.key_hint: Create an SDK token at modelscope.cn/my/myaccesstoken. Tokens look like ms-... (docs: modelscope.cn/docs/model-service/API-Inference/intro)
modelscope._note: OpenAI-compatible. GET /v1/models answers 200 without a key in the plain {"data": [...]} shape (35 models as of September 2026), so no models_url override is needed. The free tier is an account-wide allowance of 2,000 requests/day aggregated across all models, recorded below as free_allowance rather than as per-model free_limits. That figure is corroborated across several independent third-party trackers; ModelScope's own limits page is client-rendered and could not be read directly. The per-model daily cap is reported inconsistently across those same sources (200 vs 500 requests/day), so no per-model free_limits are claimed.

aion-labs.key_hint: Create an API key at aionlabs.ai/app/api-keys (docs: aionlabs.ai/docs/api-reference)
aion-labs._note: OpenAI-compatible. Aion's API reference documents GET /v1/models as requiring no authentication and returning its array under a top-level "models" key rather than "data"; llmproxy's discovery normalizes that shape, so no models_url override is needed. Four models as of September 2026 (aion-2.0, aion-3.0, aion-3.0-mini, aion-rp-llama-3.1-8b), tuned for reasoning and for roleplay/storytelling. Pay-as-you-go, no free tier.

agnes-ai.key_hint: Create an API key in the Agnes console at platform.agnes-ai.com → API Key management. Keys look like sk-... (docs: wiki.agnes-ai.com)
agnes-ai._note: OpenAI-compatible multimodal gateway. GET /v1/models is key-gated (it answers 401 'Token not provided', where an unknown /v1 path answers 404), which is what llmproxy already sends, so no models_url override is needed. The catalog also carries image and video model ids (agnes-image-*, agnes-video-*) that cannot serve chat/completions, and paid text models (agnes-2.5-pro at $0.45/$0.90 per Mtok, agnes-2.5-pro-beta at $0.10/$0.30); example_model_filter therefore pins the three free flash models. Agnes's own pricing page lists agnes-2.5-flash and agnes-3.0-flash at $0 across every billing item, and its model catalog lists agnes-2.0-flash as free-tier eligible. Rate limits are published per tier as a 'public' figure and a lower 'actual executable' one: free-tier flash text models are 30 public / 20 executable RPM (enterprise 60/40, Token Plan 1,000). free_limits records the executable figure, since that is the one a proxy must not exceed. agnes-3.0-flash postdates the published catalog and carries no limits of its own, so the flash-class figure is applied to it; its model page documents 512K context, 65,536 max output, text and image-URL input, and tool calling.
